text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parties set to spend C$100 million: Federal campaign has become a high-stakes business for major contenders, fringe groups.
- Woods youngest to master Augusta: Record setter first black victor.
- Surgery cuts risk of breast cancer: Radical treatment still controversial.
- Illness flows from tap, lurks at grocer: Ailments linked to era of exotic choices in food and travel.
- Pox on both Ottawa, PQ, Bertrand tells top court.
- 'I know there's gold there': Geologist who found Busang site says doubters are wrong.
- Falling yen stirs trade tension: Japanese face costlier imports while cheaper raise prospect of friction over exports.
- Productivity paradox puzzles experts: Millions invested in technology have failed to spark growth in output.
- www.sports.fans.rejoice : Cal Ripken Jr. is the latest to join a lineup of superstars who are wiring up to further boost their exposure and possibly their net worth.
- Markets battered, C$ hit: Banks lead stock prices lower, telegraphing unease over equity prices and interest rates. TSE 300 off 106.47 points. Dow plunges 148.36.
- OSC sidesteps Bre-X tampering issue: task force to review assay standards.
